reason: The text contains multiple regular human characters who demonstrably exercise agency throughout the narrative. The seven daughters of the Midianite priest actively draw water and fill troughs for their sheep; they speak and interact with their father; the shepherds actively drive people away; Moses actively intervenes to help the daughters and waters their flock; the priest of Midian interrogates his daughters and makes decisions (offering his daughter Zipporah to Moses); and Zipporah participates in the marriage arrangement. The narrative is fundamentally driven by the decisions and actions of these ordinary people, not by divine fiat or passive occurrence.
